concepts.title: College Budget & Funding Planner — desktop
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset: a high-fidelity raster design preview of ONLY Section 5 of the NSEDU Indian student college-discovery homepage. Generate a fresh image. No header, logo bar, browser chrome, footer, surrounding page sections, device frame, perspective or presentation-board annotations.
Design purpose: College Budget & Funding Planner, after city/state discovery, a college table and guided eligibility. Create a refined, contemporary, professionally designed STUDENT planning worksheet. It must look distinct from those earlier layouts: no giant left editorial hero and no repeated three equal cards. Prioritize clear information, attractive restrained detail, readable text and a feasible responsive interface.
Canvas/composition: wide landscape approximately 1800 x 820. Flat front-facing UI screenshot, centered 1480px-style content with generous balanced outer margins, compact section height, 8px spacing rhythm. Top small eyebrow "NSEDU / COLLEGE BUDGET". Below, elegant 42px serif heading "Know the cost. Plan with confidence." and one calm 17px line "Tuition is just the start. Include living costs and explore funding options." A quiet "Save plan" link with bookmark at far upper right.
Palette: precisely deep wine #72243B for headings and primary actions, warm taupe #806C60 as complementary accent, light ivory #FFFAF8 background, white surfaces, pale greige #F1ECE8, subtle blush #EED8DC and dark plum text #2A2024. Serif headings closely resembling DM Serif Display; controls and supporting text resemble Plus Jakarta Sans. Numbers are crisp, tabular and Indian rupee formatting is accurate. No blue, purple, green, neon, glass effects or glitter.
Main layout: a large refined planning worksheet occupying about 73% width and a narrower independent funding panel occupying 25%, with a modest gap. The worksheet is an elegant warm white surface with fine taupe/rose rules, 16px corner radii and tiny shadow, not a generic bank dashboard. Inside its top horizontal contextual band: understated college selector "Northfield Institute (demo)" with chevron; small text "B.Tech · Bengaluru · 2026–27"; a compact two-option segmented period control "First year" selected in wine and "Whole course" unselected.
Inside the worksheet, use unequal subdivisions: a narrower control rail on the left and a larger clear cost report on the right, separated by one very fine vertical rule. CONTROL RAIL: small label "First-year budget", a comfortable white input showing "₹4,00,000", a slim taupe budget slider with wine thumb and small endpoints "₹1L" / "₹6L". Then "Living arrangement" and small accessible segments "Hostel" selected, "Rental", "At home". Below a quiet "Edit assumptions" text link. Do not put every control in its own floating card.
COST REPORT: understated label "First-year estimate", prominent but balanced wine amount "₹3,75,000", a small explanation "Includes refundable deposit". A beautifully precise thin stacked cost ribbon: 64% wine, 25.6% taupe, 10.4% muted blush. Below it a neat minimal legend "Tuition" / "Living" / "Other" with matching dots. Then six compact cost entries in a two-column three-row grid, aligned labels and amounts:
"Tuition" "₹2,40,000"
"Hostel" "₹60,000"
"Meals" "₹36,000"
"Books & travel" "₹24,000"
"One-time fees" "₹10,000"
"Refundable deposit" "₹5,000".
Keep the amounts correct: these six items total ₹3,75,000. Tiny "refundable" helper belongs to the deposit, not to all fees.
Worksheet footer separated by a fine rule: a modest wine check and the readable status "₹25,000 left in your budget". Primary flat wine button "Explore colleges in my budget" and small right arrow, about 48px tall; it can occupy the row below the status if needed. No giant button or extra submit form.
FUNDING PANEL: muted greige/ivory editorial surface with a softly curved top inside corner and restrained stationery detailing, not another equal calculator card. Small label "FUNDING OPTIONS", serif title "Find ways to fund it." and a short calm line "Explore support for your next chapter." One beautifully crafted SMALL tactile cream envelope with a wine award seal or folded scholarship letter, only 90–110px high, naturally soft shadows. No money pile, coins, finance-stock imagery or huge illustration. Beneath it three very clean icon-and-text link rows with arrows: "Merit-based", "Need-based", "State schemes". An understated wine outlined button "Explore scholarships". Tiny line "Scholarships are not deducted." Do not invent awards, match counts, eligibility claims, deadlines or approved grants.
Background visual: mostly quiet ivory. Near the outer edges only, a few hairline stationery rules and one understated rounded contour suggesting a budget notebook. Tiny taupe wash around the funding artwork; no heavy blob or giant leaf, no distracting chart background. Cost visualization supplies the main creative element. Excellent typography, consistent alignment and breathable spacing.
Bottom small readable note: "Illustrative amounts. Verify programme fees before applying." The college is fictional and this is a sample design; no real institution prices or loan terms. All controls depicted are a design proposal. Render all requested English text correctly, with no gibberish or extra promotional claims. Only this section, no source references or designer commentary in the image.

concepts.title: Same budget planner — mobile reflow
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup; responsive reflow edit.
Image 1 is the desktop concept to reflow into a MOBILE design variant, not a new brand. Preserve its exact NSEDU wine #72243B, warm taupe #806C60, ivory #FFFAF8, greige, rose, DM Serif Display-like titles, Plus Jakarta Sans-like body, thin rules, cost ribbon and envelope illustration. Preserve all six cost amounts, total, budget, remaining-budget arithmetic and funding wording. Do not redesign the entire product or add features.
Produce one high-fidelity flat portrait screenshot of ONLY this section on a narrow mobile webpage. Approximately 900 x 2300 output, like a 390px CSS-width interface rendered at high pixel density, with natural vertical content. No device frame, status bar, browser UI, navigation header, footer, perspective, side-by-side alternatives or desktop layout.
Reflow professionally into ONE column with 20px-style side gutters, compact spacing and clear typography. Keep text readable at mobile scale: headline about30px CSS, body/control text14–16px, editable budget16px minimum, touch controls about44–48px. No clipped content or tiny dense desktop grid. The whole section may scroll; show the complete section in this preview.
Top small eyebrow "NSEDU / COLLEGE BUDGET", clear three-line serif heading "Know the cost. Plan with confidence.", subtitle "Tuition is just the start. Include living costs and explore funding options." A quiet compact "Save plan" link can sit beside the eyebrow.
Order: 1) context strip with single-line college dropdown "Northfield Institute (demo)", below "B.Tech · Bengaluru · 2026–27", then "First year" selected / "Whole course" tabs. 2) first-year budget label with INR input "₹4,00,000", slim slider with "₹1L" and "₹6L" endpoints; "Living arrangement", Hostel selected / Rental / At home, and "Edit assumptions". 3) prominent "First-year estimate" and "₹3,75,000", with "Includes refundable deposit". Show the same 64% wine /25.6% taupe /10.4% blush horizontal cost ribbon, legend Tuition /Living /Other. Show SIX neat full-width label/value rows rather than squeezed two-column cost cells:
Tuition — ₹2,40,000
Hostel — ₹60,000
Meals — ₹36,000
Books & travel — ₹24,000
One-time fees — ₹10,000
Refundable deposit — ₹5,000.
Keep the six amounts adding up to ₹3,75,000 and deposit refundable. 4) compact wine check/status "₹25,000 left in your budget", followed by a full-width wine button "Explore colleges in my budget" and an arrow. 5) a compact calm funding panel below, now horizontal small envelope illustration beside the title instead of huge artwork. Label "FUNDING OPTIONS", title "Find ways to fund it.", brief subtitle "Explore support for your next chapter." Three spacious link rows with small icons and arrows "Merit-based", "Need-based", "State schemes". A full-width outlined button "Explore scholarships" and small line "Scholarships are not deducted." Bottom readable note "Illustrative amounts. Verify programme fees before applying."
Keep the worksheet unified with fine rules and subtle white/greige surfaces, avoid a separate card for every row. Restrained corner-line background, mostly clear ivory. No new cost figures, no fake scholarship awards or deadlines, no blue/green/glass/neon, no repeated giant decorative shapes. This is a design image, not a working calculator.
